findings: Pool keys by allocated byte size and recycles free buffers under mutex. Contents are not zeroed on reuse; decoder failure handling previously read in Media matters before trusting returned pixels. No actual stale-pixel reproduction.

bytesPerLine arithmetic uses int width times bitsPerPixel before promotion to size_t; no checked overflow or invalid-dimension/format return visible here. Caller checks and real Qt dimension limits not fully qualified. No huge allocation or malformed-memory run.

malloc result is checked through alignment remainder rather than explicit null; null has zero remainder and may be appended to pool before returned. This is static failure-path inspection, not a reproduced OOM.

System free-memory check is advisory and separate from actual malloc success; float freeKb minus size_t reserve and integer kilobyte rounding do not provide a hard process memory budget. No claim that allocator prevents all OOM despite header wording.

_compactOnFail is set by unlocked setCompactFlag and reset outside lock after allocation, while read/reset also occurs under lock. Thread-safety of this flag requires callsite/thread confinement evidence; no data-race runtime claim.

free callback marks pointer free; no ownership/pool-membership or duplicate callback validation besides pointer assertion. Deleted destructor explicitly assumes process-lifetime allocator because QImage callbacks may outlive owner. No new ownership bug claimed without callsite evidence.
compact returns bool while compactInternal returns bytesFreed size_t, collapsing count to boolean. freeKb separately reports reusable pool size.

profile nanoTime uses gettimeofday wall clock with microsecond resolution, not monotonic nanosecond clock. Wall-clock jumps and unsigned duration subtraction can affect reported times; no performance measurement derived from logs.
